definition: lasting for a long time or constantly returning
example: Chronic illness places a heavy burden on both patients and health budgets.

definition: very severe and needing urgent attention, or starting suddenly
example: Rural hospitals face an acute shortage of experienced nurses.

definition: a widespread outbreak of a disease affecting many people at once
example: An epidemic of obesity among children is placing new pressure on paediatric services.

definition: a disease outbreak that spreads across many countries or the whole world
example: The pandemic exposed serious weaknesses in many countries' emergency planning.

definition: a sudden start of a disease or violence in a particular place
example: Health officials moved quickly to contain the outbreak by isolating infected patients.

definition: able to be passed from one person to another through contact
example: Measles is highly contagious and can spread rapidly through unvaccinated groups.

definition: an illness caused by germs entering the body
example: Washing hands regularly reduces the risk of infection.

definition: the body's ability to resist a particular disease
example: Herd immunity is achieved when enough people are protected that a disease can no longer spread easily.

definition: the giving of a substance that protects the body against a disease
example: Mass vaccination has virtually wiped out polio in most parts of the world.

definition: a medicine that kills bacteria and treats infections
example: Overuse of antibiotics has led to bacteria that no longer respond to treatment.

definition: the identification of an illness after examining the patient
example: Early diagnosis greatly improves the chances of survival for many cancers.

definition: a sign of illness that a patient feels or shows
example: The first symptom of the disease is often a persistent cough.

definition: a doctor's opinion about how an illness is likely to develop
example: The prognosis for patients diagnosed at an early stage is excellent.

definition: medical care given to a patient to cure or relieve an illness
example: Patients in remote areas often travel for hours to receive treatment.

definition: the treatment of a physical or mental problem, usually without surgery
example: Regular therapy can help people overcome anxiety without relying on medication.

definition: treatment and training that help someone return to normal life after illness or injury
example: Rehabilitation after a stroke can take many months of daily exercises.

definition: a written order from a doctor for a medicine
example: The pharmacist could not give me the tablets without a prescription.

definition: an unwanted effect of a medicine in addition to its intended one
example: Drowsiness is a common side effect of many allergy tablets.

definition: a medicine or treatment that relieves or cures an illness
example: A herbal remedy may soothe mild symptoms, but it should not replace professional care.

definition: a treatment that makes an illness disappear completely
example: Scientists have yet to find a cure for the common cold.

definition: intended to stop illness before it starts
example: Preventive care is cheaper in the long run than treating advanced disease.

definition: the average number of years a person is likely to live
example: Life expectancy has risen steadily as sanitation and medicine have improved.

definition: the number of deaths in a particular group or period
example: Infant mortality has fallen sharply since clean water reached rural villages.

definition: the condition of being so overweight that it harms health
example: Rising obesity is closely linked to cheaper processed foods and inactive lifestyles.

definition: involving a lot of sitting and little physical movement
example: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of heart disease and diabetes.

definition: a way of eating that includes the right quantities of different kinds of food
example: A balanced diet and regular exercise are the foundation of good health.

definition: poor health caused by not eating enough or not eating the right foods
example: Malnutrition stunts growth and weakens children's resistance to disease.

definition: a fatty substance in the blood that can block arteries if levels are too high
example: High cholesterol can often be reduced through changes in diet.

definition: abnormally high blood pressure
example: Hypertension frequently goes undetected because it rarely produces obvious symptoms.

definition: a disease in which the body cannot control the level of sugar in the blood
example: Type 2 diabetes is increasingly diagnosed in young adults.

definition: relating to the heart and blood vessels
example: Regular aerobic exercise strengthens the cardiovascular system and lowers the risk of heart failure.

definition: a serious loss of memory and thinking ability, mainly in old age
example: Caring for a relative with dementia can be exhausting for families.

definition: a person's emotional and psychological condition
example: Workplaces should treat mental health as seriously as physical health.

definition: a feeling of worry or fear about what might happen
example: Constant exposure to bad news can increase anxiety, particularly among teenagers.

definition: a medical condition causing persistent sadness and loss of interest in life
example: Depression often goes untreated because people are reluctant to seek help.

definition: extreme tiredness and loss of motivation caused by too much stress over a long time
example: Doctors working long shifts are at high risk of burnout.

definition: the state of being comfortable, healthy and content
example: Time spent outdoors has been shown to improve psychological well-being.

definition: the inability to stop using a substance or doing something harmful
example: Treating addiction requires support as well as willpower.

definition: the harmful use of drugs or alcohol
example: Substance abuse among teenagers is often a response to stress or peer pressure.

definition: breathing in smoke from other people's cigarettes
example: Passive smoking can cause serious respiratory problems in children.

definition: the dried leaves smoked or chewed for their nicotine
example: Raising the tax on tobacco has been shown to reduce smoking, particularly among young people.

definition: the practice of keeping clean to prevent disease
example: Strict hygiene in kitchens is essential to avoid food poisoning.

definition: the systems that provide clean water and safely remove human waste
example: Poor sanitation remains a leading cause of infectious disease in developing regions.

definition: the health of the community as a whole, and the efforts to protect it
example: Public health campaigns have successfully reduced smoking in many countries.

definition: the services provided to maintain or improve people's health
example: Access to affordable healthcare should be a basic right for every citizen.

definition: the first level of medical help that a person receives, usually from a local doctor
example: Strong primary care keeps patients out of hospital and reduces overall costs.

definition: a list of people who are waiting to receive treatment or a service
example: The waiting list for hip operations has grown to more than a year in some areas.

definition: a patient who visits a hospital for treatment but does not stay overnight
example: As an outpatient, she visited the clinic every week for physiotherapy.

definition: medical treatment that involves cutting the body to repair or remove a part
example: Many patients recover faster after keyhole surgery than after traditional operations.

definition: an operation in which an organ is replaced with one from another person
example: A kidney transplant can give patients years of life that dialysis cannot.

definition: a test given to people who have no symptoms to find disease early
example: Routine screening for breast cancer has saved thousands of lives.

definition: a general medical examination to check that you are healthy
example: I have a check-up at the dentist every six months.

definition: the finding of a disease at its first stage, before it spreads
example: Early detection allows doctors to treat tumours before they spread.

definition: relating to genes or inherited characteristics
example: Genetic factors play a role in many cancers, although lifestyle also matters.

definition: passed from parents to children through genes
example: Some forms of heart disease are hereditary and appear in several generations of one family.

definition: a medical condition in which the body reacts badly to a normally harmless substance
example: I have an allergy to pollen, so spring is difficult for me.

definition: the body's natural defence against infection and disease
example: Sleep and a nutritious diet help to strengthen the immune system.

definition: a continuing difficulty in falling or staying asleep
example: Stress and late-night screen use can both contribute to insomnia.

definition: extreme tiredness caused by effort or illness
example: Driver fatigue is a major cause of road accidents on long journeys.

definition: treatment that eases pain and discomfort for people with incurable illness
example: Palliative care focuses on dignity and comfort rather than cure.

definition: describing an illness that cannot be cured and will lead to death
example: Terminal patients are often offered the choice to spend their final weeks at home.

definition: the deliberate ending of a person's life to relieve suffering
example: The legalisation of euthanasia remains a deeply divisive ethical issue.

definition: treatments that are not part of conventional science-based medicine, such as acupuncture
example: Many people turn to alternative medicine when standard treatments have failed.

definition: a harmless substance given as medicine to test or produce a psychological effect
example: Half the participants received a placebo so that researchers could compare outcomes.

definition: a person trained to give emergency medical treatment, usually in an ambulance
example: The paramedic stabilised the patient at the roadside before transferring her to hospital.

definition: a room in a hospital with beds for patients
example: She spent a week on the surgical ward after the operation.

definition: an illness that is usually not serious
example: Pharmacists can advise on minor ailments such as coughs and sore throats.

definition: a medical condition in which the normal functions of body or mind are disturbed
example: An eating disorder can affect people of any age and background.

definition: to become worse over time
example: His condition began to deteriorate after he stopped taking the medication.

definition: to recover from illness or injury gradually
example: Patients need several weeks to recuperate after major surgery.

definition: a return of an illness after a period of improvement
example: Regular check-ups are essential to reduce the risk of relapse.

definition: making someone very weak and unable to do normal activities
example: Chronic migraines can be so debilitating that sufferers cannot work.

definition: likely to cause death
example: Food allergies can sometimes lead to a life-threatening reaction.

definition: causing the death of a person or animal
example: Without prompt treatment, the infection can prove fatal.

definition: likely to be affected by a disease or influence
example: Elderly people are particularly susceptible to pneumonia during the winter months.

definition: likely to suffer from something or to do it
example: Children who sleep badly are more prone to infections.

definition: feeling slightly ill or not quite well
example: I'm feeling a bit under the weather, so I'm going to stay at home tonight.

definition: concerned about staying healthy, especially through diet and exercise
example: Health-conscious shoppers now read nutritional labels before buying anything.

definition: a harmful loss of water from the body
example: Dehydration can cause headaches and dizziness during hot weather.
